Since demands for more transparent moderation seem to be the most requested ones, here's my idea:

Messages that are removed by mods go into a sort of limbo, viewable by the entire subverse. Ideally, this buffer would fill up with spam and offtopic comments, but should the mods go rogue and try to hide any wrongdoings, it would be immediatly obvious. Of course, said buffer would be editable by the admins only, and have a fixed quota, so that the new removed comments bump and delete old ones.

The only problem would be links to illegal content, such as child pornography. In that case the mod should have a "remove illegal content" button, where such links are removed and an admin is notified.
Comments removed by mods should go into the "removed comments" section.

Or mods get the option to hide comments which is the same as heavily downvoted comments. You can still watch them, however they need to be clicked on. The way it works is that only illegal comments like doxxing and cp is removed and off-topic stuff is hidden. This prevents comment graveyards
And make it so comments that get deleted get replaced with the reason it was deleted.

with the reason it was deleted.

This going in the public mod log at least.
Where submissions or comments with links are removed, the links should be stripped of html. No link juice for spammers!

I think it would be a good time to mention that report reasons should also be tailored for each sub. This was actually mentioned recently in /r/ideasfortheadmins. Instead of the mod having to go to the trouble of typing out the removal reason, he can just select one of the report reasons already filled in by a user. If it hasn't been reported, then he can either choose one of his sub's (or site-wide) boiler plate reasons or fill in an ad hoc one.

Those comment graveyards are probably a combination of either lazy modding, or being overwhelmed by the traffic, and just deciding to kill the whole comment chain.

There seems to be a general agreement that whatever happens moderation transparency is a high priority as it is one of the primary things that has destroyed Reddit.

In the spirit of that I've been kicking around this idea, when a user creates a sub, a mirror sub is created by the server on the /m/suffix, so in the case of here /m/ideasforvoat. This sub has no downvoting, no discussion or link posting, no mods, only the ability to comment and up vote. The sub only contains posts removed by the sub moderators. Users have to, like the main site, reach a yet to be determined threshold to participate in appeal votes and comments, and even then there is a determined limit per interval for the votes and probably just one comment on a removal being appealed, no replies everyone gets one comment, including the mod who removed it and the poster who was removed. A certain amount of appeal votes restores the thread.

I also think that if anything has to be removed from /m/ for being illegal or what not, it should appear as some sort of point in the queue with no details, but says admin removal and the reason why.
